terms.comment: Plain prose says what is hidden or unknown: rēs occulta, rēs obscūra; “it’s a mystery to me” is nesciō quō pactō factum sit or mīrum est.

evidence: Cic. Fin. 2.85: quīcum arcāna, quīcum occulta omnia (Lewis & Short, s.v. arcānus)
terms.comment: The neuter of arcānus, “kept close”: a secret, especially one kept or sacred; rare in Cicero.

terms.gloss: a secret rite; a secret; (Church) a mystery
evidence: Cic. Att. 4.18.1: epistulae nostrae tantum habent mystēriōrum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The secret rites of Eleusis; in Cicero’s letters, jokingly, a secret; in Church Latin a truth beyond human understanding and a sacrament.

sources: Lewis & Short: occultus · Lewis & Short: arcanus · Lewis & Short: mysterium
